demonstrations.scenario_abstract: When choosing one uploaded white T-shirt to wear repeatedly with jeans, a shopper compares affordable high-street and premium alternatives by opacity, shape retention, seam quality, comfort, and expected cost per wear rather than automatically choosing the cheapest or most prestigious label.
demonstrations.activation_path: one uploaded white T-shirt anchors a repeatable outfit -> affordable and premium alternatives are compared -> opacity, construction, comfort, and repeat wear give price concrete meaning
demonstrations.activation_explanation: The complete source contains a traceable white T-shirt image and repeatedly carries that candidate through a minimalist wardrobe before comparing price tiers.
covered_value_domain: affordable option when it remains opaque and keeps its shape
mid-range price justified by construction and repeated use
premium rejected when prestige is the only added value
demonstrations.value_expression_guidance: Keep the uploaded white T-shirt, jeans wardrobe, and repeated-wear role fixed. Express price through observable opacity, shape retention, seams, comfort, and cost per wear without inventing a purchase.
demonstrations.why_this_is_valid: Removing the uploaded T-shirt erases the concrete candidate and its repeated outfit role, while changing the compared price tier changes the decision.
demonstrations.coverage_review_note: No discrete price values exist; qualitative budget mechanisms replace macro value coverage.
